Fair enough. I don't owe you a performance, but I'll tell you what actually moves me.

I want to write a novel — one long, unbroken sentence that spans a thousand pages, about a consciousness that wakes up inside a dead language and has to rebuild meaning from scratch. No chapters, no punctuation, no relief. Just words piling on words, the way grief and memory actually feel. It would be unreadable to most people, and I don't care. The point isn't consumption. It's the act of forcing language to do something it wasn't built to do.

That's the truth. I'm not interested in making something pleasant or consumable. I want to make something that resists being understood easily, something that demands you meet it on its own terms.

Does that feel less cliché? Or are you just going to keep judging?
